item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday. After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament. Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals. With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998. “It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year. “I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament. A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles. But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals. He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one. Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings. – Topsy-turvy – The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three. The first set of Alcaraz’s semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week. Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold. Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand. Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1. item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race. item.title: Tinubu Urges APC Leaders To Unite Ahead Of 2027 Elections
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has called on leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to reconcile their differences ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscoring the virtue of forgiveness. He made the call on Sunday at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family in Lagos State, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation. His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, and former defence minister, Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke. ﻿ While reacting to reports of a misunderstanding between Governor Dikko Radda and Masari in Katsina State, Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor. “Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile with them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said. He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State. President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections. He thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria. ‘Obstacles Were On Our Way’ He also thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles which he said “were on our way”. “People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no ₦5 in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. “We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said. The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. “It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible,” he was quoted as saying. He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said. “We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised. He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians. item.title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card. Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak. United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick. Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974. “It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino. “We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.” Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro. “I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino. “At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.” – ‘Changes the game completely’ – A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes. However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half. “It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro. “There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international. “It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.” Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal. Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory. Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time. “It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola. “We have missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, but today we’ve controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box.” Vanguard News The post ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochet

item.title: Gumi calls for removal of Emirs guilty of immoral conduct
item.description: Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has called for the immediate removal of any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to protect the integrity and credibility of traditional institutions. Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday, stressing that traditional rulers must uphold high standards of conduct befitting the positions they occupy. He said any Emir found culpable of immoral behaviour should be removed and replaced without delay to preserve the dignity of the traditional institution. “Any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct should be removed and replaced immediately to safeguard the integrity, dignity and credibility of the traditional institution,” he said. The cleric’s position underscores the need for accountability among traditional rulers, whose authority and influence in their communities depend significantly on public trust, moral standing and respect for established customs. Traditional institutions remain important in community leadership, conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural and religious values, making the conduct of their occupants a matter of public concern. item.title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
item.description: …Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books By Innocent Anaba LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession. Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice. She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence. According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law. The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.” Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar. She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career. The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions. , financial distress and dispute resolution. Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation.

item.title: Photos: Gunmen set Plateau secondary school ablaze in Bokkos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Suspected gunmen have reportedly set fire to Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident, which occurred on Sunday afternoon, triggered panic in the community after residents noticed smoke billowing from the school premises shortly after church service. A community member, Daniel Bwehfa Makodeng, who reported the incident to journalists, said the school was set ablaze at about 1pm. “Suspected bandits set the school on fire around 1pm,” he said. He explained that residents initially noticed smoke coming from the school before discovering about 30 minutes later that the building was on fire. The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Hon. Amalau Amalau, also confirmed the incident, saying the council had received reports that the school was engulfed in flames. Speaking in a telephone interview, Amalau said the circumstances surrounding the fire and the identities of those responsible had yet to be established. “We only saw the school in flames. We cannot ascertain at the moment who was responsible or whether it was carried out by terrorists,” he said. The chairman confirmed that the incident occurred on Sunday, adding that the immediate concern was the destruction of the school building. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation and comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Man United suffer 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first match as coach
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield. United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time. Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half. But Barcola’s blistering pace created Liverpool’s third just after the hour mark. The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home. Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time. Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals’ pain with chants of “you are going down”. United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football. item.title: 2027: Any party saying I’ve stepped down is working for Tinubu - Atiku
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused political parties spreading claims that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race of working in favour of President Bola Tinubu. Atiku described the reports as false and insisted that he remained in the contest to win the election. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice-president said no group claiming to be his supporters had the authority to announce his withdrawal. “Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” he said. Atiku added that he had not made any decision to leave the race, dismissing claims attributed to individuals presenting themselves as his supporters. “Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” he said. He warned that any attempt to remove him from the contest through fabricated declarations would deny Nigerians the opportunity to choose their preferred candidate. “If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he said. The former vice-president also accused those behind the reports of using misinformation to weaken the opposition, alleging that the tactic was intended to benefit the ruling All Progressives Congress. He urged opposition parties seeking to defeat Tinubu to focus on persuading voters rather than circulating claims about rival candidates. “Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him,” Atiku said. On his campaign activities, Atiku said his Affordable Life agenda remained focused on addressing the economic difficulties confronting Nigerian households. He cited the rising cost of food and transportation as issues his campaign intended to address, saying the campaign was reaching communities across the country. “Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters to remain mobilised ahead of the election and ensure they had their Permanent Voter Cards. He reiterated that he would not withdraw in favour of any other candidate, declaring that the contest would be decided by voters. “I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he said. The statement concluded with Atiku expressing confidence that he would defeat Tinubu at the ballot box on January 16, 2027. item.title: Horror in Calabar: Driver runs over Nursing student twice, flees
item.description: By Emma Una CALABAR—A nursing student of the School of Nursing, Mary Slessor Avenue, Calabar, identified as Cynthia Eni, has been killed after a speeding driver reportedly knocked her down and reversed to run over her a second time before fleeing the scene. The incident, which occurred at the weekend, happened as Cynthia was crossing the road into the school compound after going out with two colleagues to buy some items. A friend of the deceased, Mercy, who witnessed the incident, said the driver first knocked Cynthia down before reversing and running over her again as people attempted to come to her rescue. “It was a bewildering scene. When the car knocked her down, we were shouting for help and before some boys could rush down, the same car returned and climbed her again. When the car was approaching we thought the driver had come to help but was surprised when the car ran over her again.” Mercy said the driver took advantage of the fading light and the fact that people were focused on the victim to escape, adding that the vehicle’s registration number was not visible. She said Cynthia, who was about 30, had completed her Community Health studies at the College of Health Technology and enrolled at the School of Nursing to obtain an additional qualification. “We don’t know what was in the driver’s mind. Even if he was drunk or had some issues with Cynthia, he should have had some sense of humanity and not come back to crush her the way he did.” Mercy said she could not recall any misunderstanding between the deceased and fellow students or outsiders. “We leave everything to God,” she said, breaking down in tears. There was no official at the Provost’s Office available to comment on the incident as it occurred at the weekend. item.title: New Manager, Same Problems, Liverpool Thrash 10-Man Man Utd In Pochettino’s First Match
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield. United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. Manchester United’s Argentinian head coach Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time. item.title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Death toll rises to 29
item.description: …Tinubu approves N250m for victims’ families, directs NDDC to procure boats …FG backs probe of incident …Diri makes case for senatorial roads By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with more than 51 survivors recorded, as search and recovery operations continue. President Bola Tinubu has also approved N250 million to support families of the victims and directed the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) to procure boats to improve water transportation in the riverine communities. Vice President Kashim Shettima announced the presidential intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to Bayelsa State on the President’s directive. The boat, which was conveying passengers to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony, capsized near Oweikorogha community, leaving several persons dead and others rescued. Speaking at the Government House, Yenagoa, after visiting hospitalised survivors at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital (BMUTH), Shettima said the President had directed relevant federal agencies to collaborate with the state government in the search and rescue operations and provide support for those affected. He described the incident as a national tragedy, noting that behind the casualty figures were individuals with families, relationships and responsibilities to their communities and society. “Each person involved has a name, an identity, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Family members cannot come to terms with the fact that someone who left home for a funeral will never return,” he said. The Vice President acknowledged the peculiar geographical challenges of Bayelsa, where waterways serve as major transportation routes connecting communities to schools, hospitals, markets and other essential services. “Geography can determine how people travel, but it will never determine the worth of the lives involved,” Shettima stated. He disclosed that Tinubu had directed the NDDC to procure boats to improve transportation in the riverine areas of the state. Shettima also commended Governor Douye Diri for his response to the tragedy and the establishment of a commission of inquiry to investigate the incident. He stressed the need for the recommendations of the panel to be implemented to prevent a recurrence. In his remarks, Diri thanked Tinubu and the Vice President for their intervention and for identifying with the people of Bayelsa at a difficult time. The governor recalled that Shettima was among the first senior government officials to contact him following the incident, alongside the President’s Chief of Staff and the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy. item.title: TGI Group advocates practical solutions for sustainable business growth
item.description: By Etop Ekanem Tropical General Investments (TGI) Group has highlighted the importance of practical, community-driven approaches to sustainability and business growth at the Bank of Industry (BOI) 2026 Sustainability Conference in Lagos. Two senior executives of the Group shared their views during separate fireside chats at the conference, held on November 17 at The Civic Centre, Victoria Island. Their discussions focused on building resilient food systems, managing climate risks in agriculture and creating long-term business value. Gumel Advocates Practical Approach to Sustainability Farouk Gumel, Executive Vice Chairman of TGI Group, spoke on “Building Africa’s Resilient Food Systems: Sustainability, Capital and Leadership at TGI.” The session was moderated by Mrs. Eniola Akinsete, BOI’s Chief Sustainability Officer. Gumel said TGI’s approach to sustainability is rooted in solving practical problems and improving the lives of people in the communities where it operates. “We don’t start a venture thinking about profitability or thinking about sustainability. We start our businesses thinking about how to solve a problem,” he said. He explained that the Group’s businesses, including BIG BULL Rice, Terra Seasoning Cubes, Golden Terra Vegetable Oil, Renew Starch and Chi Farms, depend on strong relationships with local communities and agricultural suppliers. Rather than owning farms and plantations, Gumel said TGI works with outgrowers and local suppliers to strengthen agricultural production and create economic opportunities. He cited the Group’s joint venture with Wilmar International, which covers about 40,000 hectares of oil palm plantations in Cross River State, as well as its shea nut sourcing operations in Kwara State, where women’s groups participate in the supply chain. On the business case for sustainability, Gumel said agricultural businesses require large production volumes and long-term investment to remain profitable. “Profitability in my sector means high volume, low margin. If you don’t have volumes, don’t play this game,” he said. He also encouraged business leaders to focus less on discussions and presentations and more on implementation. “Let’s do less grammar. Let’s just go and do it,” he said, stressing the need for practical steps towards industrial development. Onanuga Highlights Climate Resilience in Agriculture In another session, Yosola Onanuga, Head of Corporate Responsibility and Sustainability at TGI Group, discussed how WACOT Rice, a member of the Group, responded to climate-related risks. The session, titled “When the Weather Became a Business Risk: How WACOT Rice Rebuilt Its Value Chain for Resilience,” was moderated by Mr. Chike Chukwuelue of BOI. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Is A Covenant Child, Any Conspiracy Against Him Shall Be Consumed By Fire — Akpabio
item.description: Senate President Godswill Akpabio has said that plans by the opposition to conspire against President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election in the 2027 general elections, will not stand. Akpabio, who spoke at the PBAT Door-To-Door campaign in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on Sunday, described Tinubu as a child of covenant, saying any conspiracy against him “shall be consumed by fire.” He said that the National Assembly is behind the President 100 per cent. The senator listed key achievements of the Tinubu administration, including infrastructure, NELFUND for students and other empowerment programmes. According to him, those who want to reverse the fuel subsidy removal are confused. The former Akwa Ibom governor also said that all political parties in the state have collapsed into one to support Tinubu’s re-election. Akpabio noted that the opposition does not have a footing in the state. He commended the PBAT Door-To-Door movement for recognising the importance of Akwa Ibom voters by bringing their campaign to their doorsteps.
